ns2:section.sectionText: Contextuality is a property of systems of random variables as they are encountered in problems from quantum mechanics to psychology to social organizations. It characterizes the ways to reconcile observations across varying contexts, such as several experimental conditions or different studies aimed at verifying the predictions of a theory. This seminar will present a systematic introduction to the notion of contextuality, its mathematical theory, and some of its applications. Some familiarity with probability theory and linear algebra is desirable; students who have taken PSYC 506 or PSYC 594 likely have sufficient background.
